dossier: Day 4. The learner can explain promises but confuses microtask checkpoints with rendering opportunities. No cumulative browser trace exists yet.
Day 18. History and bfcache are practiced. The learner needs a production navigation failure investigation and progressive-enhancement decision.
Day 6. Structural typing is practiced. The learner previously exposed an unreadable generic component API and needs to understand assignability.
Day 20. Runtime validation boundaries are practiced. The learner must choose between handwritten, generated, and schema-first validation.
Day 8. The learner knows rendering vocabulary but has not made route-level decisions from latency, cache, accessibility, and ownership evidence.
Day 21. Security trust boundaries are practiced. The learner needs an explicit browser, BFF, identity-provider, and refresh failure model.
Day 3. The learner has used codemods but cannot explain concrete syntax trees, source ranges, or safe transformation invariants.
Day 28. Bundler graphs and deterministic CI are practiced. The learner needs a measured migration and rollback artifact for a large monorepo.
The learner is new to distributed systems and equates availability with a host being powered on. Use a concrete partition timeline and avoid unexplained consistency vocabulary.
The learner knows replication and hash rings but has not stated how concurrent versions and node failure affect returned values. Require a falsifiable consistency contract.
The learner can navigate directories but has only used filenames without spaces. Teach argument boundaries before introducing any file-changing operations in the lab.
The learner already uses pipelines and permissions but mistakes temporal correlation for proof. Require command evidence and comparison of two hypotheses from supplied logs.
The learner uses functions and arrays but assumes set -e catches every failure. Require a conditional-context example and preservation of the original exit status.
The learner has practiced automation and recovery. Require concrete tests for empty input, unusual filenames, interruption and repeat execution before claiming the tool is reliable.
